title: On two conjectures of Hoàng
summary: A graph $G$ is said to be perfectly divisible if for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ with at least one edge, the vertex set $V(H)$ can be partitioned into two sets $A, B$ such that $H[A]$ is perfect and $ω(B) < ω(H)$. It is easy to see that the chromatic number of a perfectly divisible graph is at most $\binom{ω(G)+1}{2}$. Hoàng conjectured that every graph $G$ with $α(G) \le 3$ is perfectly divisible.
